Four sites in Madhya Pradesh that together span prehistoric rock art, early Buddhist architecture, Gupta sculpture and the medieval temple at its height. An archaeologist leads the tour, and reading is sent in advance.

A day-by-day itinerary and a quotation are shared before you commit. Route, pace, accommodation and budget are adjusted to suit your group.

What it covers

  • Bhimbetka: painted rock shelters
  • Bhojpur and Sanchi: an unfinished temple and the Great Stupa
  • Udayagiri: rock-cut caves of the Gupta period
  • Khajuraho: the Chandella temples

Day by day

  1. Day 1: Bhopal

    Arrival, and the State Museum for the region's archaeology in one place.

  2. Day 2: Bhimbetka and Bhojpur

    Painted rock shelters in the morning; the unfinished Bhojeshwar temple in the afternoon.

  3. Day 3: Sanchi

    The Great Stupa, its four gateways and the monasteries on the hill.

  4. Day 4: Udayagiri and Vidisha

    Gupta-period rock-cut caves and the old city beside them.

  5. Day 5: To Khajuraho

    A long road day across Madhya Pradesh.

  6. Day 6: Khajuraho

    The Western Group of Chandella temples: plans, towers and sculpture.

  7. Day 7: Khajuraho and departure

    The Eastern and Southern groups, then the flight or train home.

Days can be added, removed or reordered. The final itinerary comes with your quotation.

By the end you can

  • Describe the painted rock shelters of Bhimbetka and the unfinished Bhojeshwar temple.
  • Describe the Great Stupa at Sanchi, its four gateways and the monasteries on the hill.
  • Read the plans, towers and sculpture of the Chandella temples at Khajuraho.

You take away

Daily field sheets and a final comparative portfolio.
